# Background

# Methods {#sec-data-methods}

## Study design

piano group and active control group

Blood samples were taken at three different time points. The first (T0) one week before the weekly cycle of practical or theoretical music lessons were started. The second (T1) after 6 months and the third (T2) again after 6 months so one year after T0.

Because multiple tests were performed on each inidivuals time point (not only blood samples but also fMRI as part of the original study) T0 fell between March and June 2019, T1 between August 2019 and February 2020 and T2 between June 2020 and November 2020.

Auch in meiner Untersuchung? *A small subgroup of participants were recruited as early as in January 2019 (T0), and had their consecutive examinations in August 2019 (T1) and in the end of February/beginning of March 2020 (T2). In other words, their T2 was directly before the lockdown started. Therefore, this small subgroup was excluded from the main analyses*

## Study participants

The participants of the study cohort were recruted at the Geneva Musical Minds Lab, Geneva School of Health Sciences, University of Applied Sciences and Arts Western Switzerland (HES-SO), Geneva, Switzerland and the Hannover Medical School, Dept. for Clinical Psychiatry, Social Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, Division of Clinical Psychology and Sexual Medicine in corporation with the Institut für Musikphysiologie und Musiker-Medizin Hochschule für Musik, Theater und Medien affiliated to the Hochschule für Musik, Theater und Medien Hannover. Possibility for participation was made public through newspaper advertisement and posters in public places. Table 1 summarizes relevant demographic information about the study cohort. Some requirements had been to be met for volunteers to participate in the study. They had to be in overall good health, right-handed, retired and not relying relieingon hearing aids.

## Measurement of DNA methylation

### Target Genes

We focused on the primer regions of three genes commonly neuroplasticity-associated and hypthecised being potentially epigenetically modifiable by playing the piano: BDNF4, PSD95, MAPT (Tau).

### DNA isolation

Genomic DNA (gDNA) was isolated at the Institute of Molecular and Translational Therapeutic Strategies of Hannover Medical School from 50 µL blood using the "NucleoMag Blood 200 µl" kit (MACHEREY-NAGEL GmbH & Co. KG, Düren, Deutschland) in concordance with the instructions of the manufacturer. The isolated gDNA was stored at -20 °C. The blood samples have been received anonymized and prior to gDNA isolation. Then the samples were additionaly randomized *(by doing what?)* to minimize potential batch effects. DNA samples were diluted in 96-well plates to a fixed concentration of 10 ng/µl.

### Bisulfite Conversion

The gDNA of all samples was then bisullfite converted via the "EZ-96 DNA Methylation-Lightning™ MagPrep" kit (Zymo Research Corporation, Irvine, CA, USA) also following the manufacturers instructions.

### Primer design

With Ensembl and Geneious Pro 5.6.7 the primer regions of our target genes were located and the sequences of the primer regions analyzed. Aided by Biocalculator (metabion), NetPrimer (Premier Biosoft), Methyl Primer Express v1.0 (Applied Biosystems) and Bisulfite Primer Seeker (Zymo) we designed primers for PCR with bisulfite-converted DNA (see Table 1) and sequencing primers (Table 2) - later used to prepare Sanger Sequencing - and orderd these primers from metabion GmbH (Martinsried, Deutschland).

### Gene Amplification

The primers were dissolved in nuclease-free water. The proportions have been predetermined by the manufacturer. The stock solution 100 pmol. It was then used to derive a working solution of 20 pmol (1:5). Both solutions were prexserved atg -20 °C. Amplification was then performed together with HotStarTaq® PCR Master Mix Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Deutschland). The samples were then puriefed with the PCR purification kit "CleanNGS" (CleanNA, Waddinxveen, Niederlande).

### Sanger Sequencing

The purfied PCR prodcus were sequenced with the BigDye Terminator v3.1 Cycle Sequencing Kit (Applied Biosystems, Foster City, CA, USA) and the sequencing primers mentioned above (Table 2). The sequencing product were purifed with the "CleanDTR" kit (CleanNA, Waddinxveen, Niederlande).

Then using the Applied Biosystems' 3500 Genetic Analyzer (ABI 3500xL) Capillary electrophoresis was performed.

### Data Processing via ESME

The data derived from the ABI 3500xL was then processed with Epigenetic Sequencing Methylation (ESME) analysis software.

## Data Structuring and Statistical Analysis

For data structuring and transformation Excel, SPSS and R (4.5.2), *using the following packages: tidyverse, dplyr, readxl ...* . After structuring the data, R (4.5.2) was used to analyze the data. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was done with the prcomp package (...). Descriptive statistics we perforemd using the ... Plots were designed using the ggplot2 and ... package.

We performed modelling with 3 different types of models. Linear models. The difference of 2 time points was modelled (T2 - T0, T1 - T0 and T2 - T1) and after that used as the depenedet variable.

Generalized Linear model (GLM) with the ... package

Lastly Zero-Inflated Beta Distribution Regression Models with random effects (ZIBR) were performed using the glmmTMB package for modelling and DHARMa for residual diagnostics.

## Principal component analysis

Showed that specific CpGs drove the variance specifically for Tau and PSD95. Assessing the covariacne matrix, large differences in variance between the CpGs were seen.

## Methylation Levels

-   Die Gene sind allgemein eher gering methyliert (Mean \< 0,08, Median \< 0,04). **Hohe Expressionsrate!**
-   Dabei ist PSD95 am geringsten und BDNF am höchsten metyhyliert.
-   Bei Tau sind die CpGs promoterfern mehr meyhtliert - bei PSD95 umgekehrt (*Boxplots mit CpG-Methylierung der Gene!*)
-   **Lagemaß u. Streuungsmaß?**

### Group differences

Our main goal we aimed to determine whether the degree of methylation differed between the intervention (piano lessons) and control groups.

-   Bei BDNF zeigt sich eine leichte Differenz zwischen der Kontrollgruppe (Median: 0.07, Mean: 0.07326) und der Pianogruppe (Median: 0.064, Mean: 0.06598), welche eine niedrigere Metyhlierung (Median: -0.006, Mean: -0.00728) aufwies. **Streuungsmaße?**
-   Weiterhin zeigen sich für die arithmetischen Mittel von BDNF und PSD95 zwei Modi.
-   Tau war unimodal.

### Time differences

-   Bei BDNF zeigt sich, dass sich die Mittelwerte (Arithmetisch und Median) von T0 zu T1 leicht absenken und zu T2 wieder über das Niveau von T0 ansteigen.
-   Bei Tau steigt das arithmetische Mittel der Methylierung leicht von T0 zu T1 und hält das Niveau bei T2.
-   Bei PSD95 verbleibt der Median der Methylierung gleichbleibend bei 0, während das arithmetische Mittel der Methylierung von T0 zu T1 steigt aber bei T2 wieder auf das Ausgangsniveau zurückfällt.

### Tests und Modelle

# Discussion

The null hypothesis of our study was that playing the piano has no effect on the methylation of neuroplasticity-associated genes like BDNF, PSD95 and Tau. Despite of Tau the null hypothesis could be rejected.
